LESSON: PATH OF ACTION (KARMA YOGA) • SISTER NIVEDITA • RISHABH DEV, • BUDDHAGHOSHA • BIBI SUNDARI JI

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.1: Path of Action (Karma Yoga) • Sister Nivedita • Rishabh dev, • Buddhaghosha • Bibi Sundari Ji
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 14

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Path of Action (Karma Yoga) • Sister Nivedita • Rishabh dev, • Buddhaghosha • Bibi Sundari Ji, part of Strand 5 in Grade 8 HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION.

Key inquiry question: How do the lives of practitioners of karma Yoga inspire us? 2. Why do we need to practise Karma Yoga?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. make a list of all the duties/roles in their life, divide them into the roles they like and dislike and prioritise as per importance at home and in school,

2. hold discussions with peers to assess each other’s daily actions with regards to Karma Yoga,

3. read key events of prominent practitioners of Karma Yoga through digital media/ assistive digital media/ library/resource persons, summarise and make a presentation on the benefits of selfless service based on their personal experience and lessons from resource persons,

4. role-play key events of prominent practitioners of Karma Yoga,

5. select relevant scriptural stories/verses/hymns that reflect on Karma Yoga, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. make a list of all the duties/roles in their life, divide them into the roles they like and dislike and prioritise as per importance at home and in school,
2. hold discussions with peers to assess each other’s daily actions with regards to Karma Yoga,
3. read key events of prominent practitioners of Karma Yoga through digital media/ assistive digital media/ library/resource persons, summarise and make a presentation on the benefits of selfless service based on their personal experience and lessons from resource persons,
4. role-play key events of prominent practitioners of Karma Yoga,
5. select relevant scriptural stories/verses/hymns that reflect on Karma Yoga, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Path of Action (Karma Yoga) • Sister Nivedita • Rishabh dev, • Buddhaghosha • Bibi Sundari Ji together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: The learner enhances listening and teamwork skills while role-playing key events of

prominent practitioners of Karma Yoga.

● Learning to learn and Critical thinking: The learner develops self-discipline when making a list of all the duties/roles in their

life, divide them into the roles they like and dislike and prioritise as per importance at home and in school.

● Digital literacy: The learner interacts with technology when reading key events of prominent practitioners of Karma Yoga

through digital media/assistive digital media.

Values:
Responsibility: The learner enhances self-drive when committing to selfless services and making a list of all the duties/roles in

their life, divide them into the roles they like and dislike and prioritise as per importance at home and in school.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCI’s):

● Global citizenship: The learner enhances global citizenship when undertaking selfless service in their school and community.

● Learner support programmes: The learner strengthens positive discipline when making a list of all the duties/roles in their

life, divide them into the roles they like and dislike and prioritise as per importance at home and in school.

Link to other subjects:

The learner can relate to the skills of role-playing key events of prominent practitioners of Karma Yoga and will develop civic

mindedness as they undertake selfless service in their school and community to the skills of role playing learnt in Social Studies.
